posts.text:
Similar to the NBA's efforts to curb tanking, this league will adopt the
"3-2-1 Lottery"
system.
How does it work?
15 teams will participate in the draft lottery:
the 13 teams that miss the playoffs, plus the two 8-seeds in each conference. All 15 picks will be drawn in the lottery.
Lottery balls will be allocated as follows:
1
The three teams with the worst records in the league will be in the
relegation zone
and receive two lottery balls each.
All other teams that miss the playoffs and finish 11th or worse in their conference will receive three lottery balls each.
The 9th- and 10th-place teams in each conference will receive two lottery balls each.
The 8-seed in each conference will receive one lottery ball each.
Relegation zone protection:
The three teams in the relegation zone cannot pick lower than 12th.
No consecutive #1 picks:
A team cannot receive the #1 overall pick in back-to-back years.
2
Top-5 pick restriction:
A team cannot receive a top-5 pick in three consecutive years.
2
Second-round order:
The first 15 picks of the second round will follow the reverse order of the first-round draft order.
Notes:
1 - Any ties affecting team groupings will be broken by a (virtual) coin flip.
2 - All lottery restrictions apply to the team that originally owned the pick, regardless of any trades.

It wouldn't be the Sports Insomnia League without a creation draft to kick things off. With that comes a few guidelines:
Draft Order
The draft order will be determined by random draw.
The draft will follow a snake format, with the order reversing in every even-numbered round.
Picks
Picks that go on the clock between 8:00 AM and 8:00 PM EST will have a four-hour clock. Picks that go on the clock outside of those hours will have an eight-hour clock, or until 12:00 PM EST that day, whichever comes first.
If your pick clock expires, you will be placed on auto-draft. You may request to come off auto-draft, but your pick windows will be shortened to two hours between 12:00 PM and 8:00 PM EST, and four hours outside of those hours.
If you miss three picks over the course of the draft, you will be placed on auto-draft for the remainder of the draft and will no longer be allowed to request to come off auto-draft.
Trades
Trading is not permitted during the draft, in any capacity.
Contracts
Drafted players will carry the contracts they had at the start of the 2005–06 NBA season.
There is no limit to the total salary a team can draft. However, any team above either apron at the conclusion of the creation draft will be subject to the applicable
apron rules
.

posts.author: CC06
posts.text:
All draft threads are for
PICKS ONLY
. Do not post in a draft thread unless your team is on the clock.
All picks must be submitted on the site. Posting a player’s name on Discord does not count as making a pick.
Once submitted, all draft picks are final.
Pick Clock
Between 12:00 PM and 8:00 PM EST, first-round picks have a four-hour clock. In this same time window, second-round picks have a two-hour clock.
If your pick is automated due to an expired clock, all your remaining picks in the current draft will also be automated.
Trading Current Picks
A pick that is currently on the clock can only be traded within the first hour of the pick coming on the clock. After that hour, the team that owns the pick must make a selection.

posts.author: CC06
posts.text:
At the start of the second round, a list will be published showing which remaining prospects are only willing to sign a guaranteed contract and which are willing to sign a two-way contract.
Guaranteed contracts count toward your team salary, while two-way contracts have no salary cost.
Picks
You cannot assign a player who is only willing to sign a guaranteed contract to a two-way deal.
If you make your own second-round pick, the player will receive a guaranteed contract unless you specifically request a two-way contract in your pick post.
If your pick is automated between picks 30 and 39, the player will automatically receive a guaranteed contract.
If your pick is automated at pick 40 or later, the player will be selected from the pool of prospects willing to accept a two-way contract.
Guaranteed Contracts
If you give a second-round rookie a guaranteed contract, you may choose from the following contract structures:
1-year rookie minimum
2-year rookie minimum (no options)
3-year minimum contract, starting at the 1-year minimum salary, with a team option in the final year
4-year minimum contract, starting at the 2-year minimum salary, with a team option in the final year
If you do not specify a contract structure for your second-round pick, the default will be a 2-year rookie minimum with no team options.
Please note that these contracts count against the salary cap and luxury tax at the amounts listed on the index. They are not treated as minimum contracts for a player with two years of league experience, as
standard one-year minimum free-agent contracts
are.

posts.author: CC06
posts.text:
Training Camp determines how players improve, stagnate, or decline each offseason. Development is influenced by age, potential, playing time, player archetype, and random variance.
Given how much of a black box the in-game training camp simulation is, along with its obvious flaws, I've decided it's finally time to move this ever-important game mechanic to an external system that can be understood and controlled.
Who Goes Through Training Camp?
Rookies skip their first Training Camp.
They enter the system after completing their first season.
G-League assignments
provide a guaranteed baseline level of development, exceeding what players receive from minimal NBA minutes.
What Drives Development?
Age:
Young players generally develop the fastest, though their results are more volatile. Development ramps up gradually for teenage players, becomes steadier in their mid-to-late twenties, and eventually gives way to decline.
Potential:
Higher potential generally means more room for development, while potential naturally decreases as a player develops. Potential is not a rating cap; players can exceed expectations through breakouts and favorable variance.
Playing Time:
Both minutes per game and games played affect development. More playing time generally means more growth, but meaningful rotation minutes still help. Young players also have a development floor to protect them from being held back by limited opportunities.
Breakout Seasons:
Players can experience unusually strong development, with chances influenced by age and potential. Breakouts come in three tiers: minor, major, and elite. Higher tiers are increasingly rare, with elite breakouts capable of dramatically changing a player's trajectory.
Season Variance:
Players may have unusually good, poor, or stagnant development seasons. Older players also face the risk of sudden, significant declines.
How Skills Develop
Skill-based attributes
such as passing, handling, shooting, and defense can improve through experience and development.
Physical attributes
follow age-related curves. Strength can improve into a player's mid-twenties, while quickness and jumping peak earlier and decline sooner.
Archetype matters.
Players develop according to their position, skill set, and existing strengths. Guards, bigs, shooters, playmakers, and defensive specialists will each develop differently.
Elite skills are harder to improve.
Players already rated highly in an attribute have less room to grow than those with lower ratings.
Physical Decline
Physical decline begins as players age, with quickness and jumping typically fading first, followed by strength. Skills that rely on athleticism may also decline.
Heavier players are more susceptible to physical breakdown later in their careers, and extra weight accelerates decline once their development window begins to close. Decline is gradual at first but becomes more pronounced with age.
The Unpredictability Is the Point
No two careers are guaranteed to follow the same path. Randomness, breakouts, and age-related changes mean players may develop faster, peak earlier, or decline differently than expected.
The system rewards smart roster management while keeping player development unpredictable and believable.

posts.author: CC06
posts.text:
It's time to restore the feeling.
Over the last few months, I've had enough people express interest in a sim league to give me hope that there's still room in the ether for another one of these things. If TSFBL III was our last dance, then we're now entering our Jordan Wizards era.
As such, this league is going to look a lot different. TSFBL was a league that required a full group of GMs to be locked in and fully committed. This time, we're taking the opposite approach. Even if we only have eight people who want to see this thing through, we'll keep it moving. This one is for the people. We're prepared to handle inactive GMs and CPU-run teams, and the overall atmosphere is going to be pretty relaxed.
I know where I am in life, and I know that not everybody has the time to commit to a league the way we might have years ago. Luckily, we have two other GMs, daulten780 and TYO, who are passionate enough about bringing this thing back to help out as assistant commissioners. They'll be taking some responsibilities off my plate and helping make things easier for everybody.
The bottom line is simple:
sim leagues should be fun.
Sports Insomnia celebrated its 20th anniversary this year, and the reason for this rebrand is to bring back that nostalgic feeling we all remember from the sim leagues we grew up with. To help recapture that experience, we're bringing back features from the old leagues, including the Creation Draft, box score claims, the G-League, and more.
We're incredibly excited to get this thing going again, and we can't wait to get started. Here are a few housekeeping notes to get us rolling:
Creation Draft
As mentioned above, just like the old Sports Insomnia leagues, we're starting with a
Creation Draft
.
We know these things can drag on. If you're someone who doesn't particularly care who's on your team at the start and just wants to get to the trading, feel free to go on auto-draft. We'll see you on the other side!
Anti-Tanking
Just like the modern NBA, we're going to do our best to curb tanking through
lottery reform
.
I know not everybody is going to click through every thread and read every rule, so I wanted to make sure this was on your radar right from the start.
Modern CBA
Just like TSFBL III, we're going to do our best to mirror the NBA's current CBA. That doesn't mean you need to learn a mountain of rules if that's not your thing. We'll help you navigate everything along the way, and the assistant commissioners are available if you have any questions.
New Training Camp System
To keep things fresh, I've created a brand-new
training camp system
that we'll be using in this league.
Depth Charts
For the regular season, depth charts will be 100% automated. When we say we're seriously trying to cut back on the level of time you have to commit to being in a sim league, we mean it.

follow age-related curves. Strength can improve into a player's mid-twenties, while quickness and jumping peak earlier and decline sooner.
Archetype matters.
Players develop according to their position, skill set, and existing strengths. Guards, bigs, shooters, playmakers, and defensive specialists will each develop differently.
Elite skills are harder to improve.
Players already rated highly in an attribute have less room to grow than those with lower ratings.
Physical Decline
Physical decline begins as players age, with quickness and jumping typically fading first, followed by strength. Skills that rely on athleticism may also decline.
Heavier players are more susceptible to physical breakdown later in their careers, and extra weight accelerates decline once their development window begins to close. Decline is gradual at first but becomes more pronounced with age.
The Unpredictability Is the Point
No two careers are guaranteed to follow the same path. Randomness, breakouts, and age-related changes mean players may develop faster, peak earlier, or decline differently than expected.
The system rewards smart roster management while keeping player development unpredictable and believable.

For both, ten days will be simmed. All
box score claims
will count. All Summer League injuries will carry over to the Preseason. All Preseason injuries will carry over to the regular season.

prospect_potential.title: Prospect Potential
prospect_potential.text:
For the first time, prospect potential will be completely dynamic and will not be determined until after a player is drafted.
Each prospect will be randomly assigned to one of four categories. Their actual potential will then be randomly generated based on the category they are assigned:
The player's historical potential
The potential associated with the player's historical draft slot
The potential associated with the player's sim league draft slot
Completely random
The scouted potential listed on the index is the player's historical potential and does not reflect their actual potential once they are drafted.
This does not apply to players in the base file.
